observations.finding: 0 of 50 pathways significant; minimum q=0.160 (UV_RESPONSE_DN SMD=-0.57).
No gene significant at q<0.05; top trends include BAP1 (23.3% vs 8.2%, OR=3.40, 95% CI 1.04-11.16, Fisher p=0.050, q=0.426) and PBRM1 (50% vs 32.9%, OR=2.04, q=0.649).

No CNV feature significant at q<0.05; top continuous effects include chr13q (Cliff's delta=0.35, q=0.246) and chr14q (delta=-0.34, q=0.246); gain/loss top includes chr14q loss (60% vs 32.9%, OR=3.06, q=0.246) and CDKN2A loss (43.3% vs 16.4%, OR=3.89, q=0.246).

key_evidence.statistical_interpretation: RNA shows no significant pathway enrichment; WXS and CNV show suggestive but non-significant trends (BAP1 mutation, chr14q/CDKN2A loss) with q-values >0.2. Effect sizes are moderate but confidence intervals are wide. Availability is complete (set n=30, rest n=73).
key_evidence.medical_interpretation: There is weak molecular support for this set, with possible genomic alterations (BAP1, CDKN2A) but no transcriptomic coherence.
limitations: No significant findings after FDR; trends are exploratory and could be due to small sample size.

Retaining this candidate for downstream validation is better supported than Drop.
